function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Next major festival in the United States (as of 2026‑09‑03)** | Festival | Dates | Location | What to Expect | Ticket Info | Official Site | |----------|-------|----------|----------------|-------------|---------------| | **New York Film Festival (NYFF)** | **September 27 – October 10, 2026** | New York City – Film Forum, Lincoln Center, and other venues | • 200+ world‑premiere and U.S. premiere films (independent, art‑house, documentaries, shorts)
• Curated “Spotlight” sections, retrospectives, and special events
• Panels, Q&A sessions with filmmakers, and industry networking | • General admission: $30–$45 (early‑bird discounts available)
• VIP packages (back‑stage access, meet‑and‑greet) start at $150
• Group rates for schools and organizations | [nyff.org](https://www.nyff.org) | ### Why NYFF is a great choice - **Timing**: It’s the first major film festival in the U.S. after the summer season, so it’s a fresh slate of new releases. - **Diversity**: The program spans all genres and formats, with a strong emphasis on international cinema and emerging voices. - **Accessibility**: Many screenings are free or low‑cost, and the festival often partners with local community centers for outreach. - **Networking**: If you’re a filmmaker, critic, or film student, the industry panels and networking events are invaluable. --- #### Other notable festivals happening soon (in case you’re looking for something different) | Festival | Dates | City | Highlights | |----------|-------|------|------------| | **South by Southwest (SXSW)** | March 10 – 19, 2027 | Austin, TX | Music, film, interactive media, tech talks | | **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | April 12 – 15, 2027 | Indio, CA | Top‑tier music acts, art installations | | **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | May 20 – 28, 2027 | New Orleans, LA | Jazz, blues, world music, cultural celebrations | | **Burning Man** | August 28 – September 6, 2027 | Black Rock Desert, NV | Art, community, self‑expression in a temporary city | --- ### Quick Tips for Planning 1. **Book Early** – Tickets for NYFF and other festivals sell out fast, especially for popular screenings. 2. **Check Accommodation** – Hotels in NYC fill up quickly during festival week; consider staying in nearby boroughs (Brooklyn, Queens) or booking a short‑term rental. 3. **Transportation** – NYC’s public transit (subway, buses) is the most efficient way to get around during the festival. 4. **Stay Informed** – Sign up for the festival’s newsletter or follow their social media for last‑minute updates, schedule changes, and special events. Enjoy the festival season! If you’d like more details on any of the events above or help with travel arrangements, just let me know.
